idea-plugin.name: DevTomcat
idea-plugin.description:
DevTomcat

Free, full-featured Apache Tomcat integration for IntelliJ IDEA. Run, debug, and deploy web applications with smart diagnostics, live status tracking, and zero configuration overhead.

Core Features

  • Full Tomcat lifecycle — start, stop, debug, and redeploy from the IDE
  • Deploy WAR files and exploded directories with auto-detected artifacts
  • Multi-artifact deployment with independent context paths
  • Debug with full breakpoint and hot-swap support
  • Code coverage with JaCoCo integration
  • Hot deployment and Update Running Application (Ctrl+F10)
  • CATALINA_BASE isolation — each configuration gets its own instance directory
  • server.xml auto-generation with HTTP, HTTPS, AJP, and shutdown connectors
  • JMX monitoring support
  • Remote deployment via Tomcat Manager API

Smart Diagnostics

  • Error Diagnostics Engine — Detects 16+ common Tomcat errors (ClassNotFound, BindException, OOM, SSL, JDBC, etc.) with categorized severity, actionable suggestions, and quick-fix IDs
  • Version Compatibility Checker — Validates Tomcat/JDK compatibility before launch (Tomcat 7–11 matrix) and warns about Jakarta EE namespace changes
  • Auto-Port Resolution — Detects port conflicts at startup and auto-resolves to available ports with console warnings

Live Deployment Dashboard

  • Live Status Tracking — Real-time server and per-artifact status (Starting, Deploying, Running, Failed) in the Services tool window
  • Run History — Persistent history of Tomcat run sessions with duration, startup time, artifact activity, and consecutive failure tracking
  • Startup Time Trends — Tracks startup performance across runs and shows trend comparisons

Enhanced Console & Config

  • Smart Console Filter — Clickable URLs (opens browser) and file paths (opens in editor) in Tomcat console output
  • Config Export/Import — Export and import run configurations as XML files for team sharing
  • Per-mode Runner Settings — Separate environment variables and startup scripts for Run, Debug, and Coverage modes
  • Multi-log Monitoring — Catalina, localhost, access, and custom log files as dedicated console tabs

Requirements

  • IntelliJ IDEA 2024.1+
  • Apache Tomcat 7+
  • Java 17+
idea-plugin.change-notes:
Version 1.0.9

Deep deployment audit. Security hardening, Tomcat-version compatibility shims, port-resolver correctness, and many smaller fixes around launch, Debug on 2025.1, and remote deploy.

Security

  • AJP without address reproduced CVE-2020-1938 (Ghostcat) — when the user enabled AJP with no existing connector, the launcher injected one with secretRequired="false" and no host binding, leaving unauthenticated AJP open on every interface. IDE-injected AJP connectors now bind to 127.0.0.1; user-configured connectors are untouched.
  • JMX exposed without host binding — when JMX was enabled the launcher set local.only=false, authenticate=false, and ssl=false, but did not pin jmxremote.host. JMX and the RMI registry now bind to 127.0.0.1 by default; an explicit -D in VM options takes precedence.

Data-loss fixes

  • copyConfDirectory deleted the user's conf/ when CATALINA_BASE equalled CATALINA_HOME — pinning the base to the registered Tomcat install hit an unguarded recreateDirectory that wiped server.xml, tomcat-users.xml, and the policy files before the copy walk. Same-path is now refused with a clear error before any destructive work runs.
  • Stale-deployment cleanup wiped pinned CATALINA_BASE — the launch-time wipe of webapps/*.war and conf/Catalina/localhost/*.xml ran indiscriminately even on user-managed installs. Cleanup is now gated to the IDE-managed system directory.
  • Parallel-run cleanup followed a symlink at the run-base root — a symbolic link planted at .runs/{runId} could redirect the recursive delete onto an unrelated tree. Switched to NOFOLLOW_LINKS with explicit refusal.

Tomcat-version compatibility (new shims)

  • BCEL "Invalid byte tag in constant pool: 19" on Tomcat 7.x / 8.0.x / 8.5.<51 / 9.0.<31 — their bundled BCEL parser does not recognise Java 9+ module-info.class and floods the run console with one stack trace per modular JAR (jackson, jaxb-api, byte-buddy, snakeyaml, etc.). New BcelModuleInfoCompat shim detects affected versions and appends modular JARs to the appropriate jarsToSkip property in catalina.properties (DefaultJarScanner on 7/8.0, StandardJarScanFilter on 8.5+). Per-context <JarScanFilter> is intentionally not used because Tomcat 7's Digester has no rule for it. Modern Tomcats untouched. Runtime classloading unchanged.
  • Pre-launch ECJ-vs-class-file compatibility check — Tomcat's bundled Eclipse JDT compiler is used by Jasper to compile JSPs; older ECJ releases can't read newer Java class files. Tomcat 7.0.30 ships ECJ 3.7.2 (Java 7 max), so any webapp with Java 8+ dependencies hits org.eclipse.jdt.internal.compiler.classfmt.ClassFormatException at request time. New EcjVersionCompat shim parses tomcat/lib/ecj-*.jar, maps version → max Java (table covering Eclipse 3.4 → 4.34), samples class file majors across WEB-INF/classes/** and WEB-INF/lib/*.jar root entries, and surfaces a single warning naming the bundled ECJ, the highest webapp class major, and the resolution paths (upgrade Tomcat / swap the ECJ JAR / lower the target).

Correctness

  • Port resolver displaced peer services with their own configured ports — when HTTP was bound and the next port matched a peer's preferred slot, the resolver either took it (knocking the peer aside) or aborted with "no alternative found". The search is now peer-aware: it skips both the running allocated set and the configured ports of unresolved peers.
  • Restart in Debug on IntelliJ 2025.1 threw IllegalStateException: Running sync tasks on pure EDT — destroyProcess now runs off-EDT. Same fix applied to the Services-panel Stop action.
  • Tomcat 7 deploy warning "No rules found matching 'Context/Resources/PreResources'" — <PreResources>/<PostResources> are Tomcat 8+; the generator now skips that block on Tomcat 7 and logs a one-line note instead.
  • Manager URL with trailing slash silently became localhost — RemoteConfig.setManagerUrl regex required no trailing slash; a natural http://host:8080/manager/ failed validation and the setter fell back to default. Setter now strips trailing slashes before validation.
  • Remote-deploy URL injection — TomcatManagerDeployer concatenated context paths into ?path= raw; a context like /myapp&update=false would inject extra query params. All three call sites now URL-encode the path.
  • Smart-error console dropped the detected message — TomcatErrorDiagnostics.formatForConsole showed only the suggestion. Format now includes the message.
  • Renaming a running config leaked its ports — the rename listener migrated status/history/startup-tracker but missed TomcatPortRegistry. Registry now exposes a renameConfiguration migration the listener calls alongside the others.
  • Carry-over relaunch lost JDWP exhaustion warnings — when the carried debug port couldn't be claimed, the relaunch silently kept the original. Now logs the same exhaustion / bump warnings as the first-time debug path.
  • Silent JRE fallback — when the configured JRE was no longer registered, the launcher fell back to project SDK with only an idea.log WARN. Fallback is now surfaced in the run console.
  • One throwing listener silenced its peers — TomcatLifecycleListener.composite and TomcatOutputPipeline.processLine ran consumers in a bare for-loop. Both now isolate per-listener with WARN logging.
  • Remote-deploy background task outlived its process — stopping the local Tomcat mid-deploy left the task running and posting stale dashboard updates. Task now short-circuits on terminating/terminated state.
  • TomcatConfigurationData.setContextPath skipped slash canonicalization — programmatic callers (XML deserializer, imported configs) could land non-slash-prefixed paths producing broken URLs. Setter now canonicalizes via ContextPathUtils.normalizeContextPath.
  • Manual-JDWP detection masked by a leading -agentlib:jdwp_other — hasManualJdwpAgent ran a single indexOf; a near-miss masked a real agent later in the string and the duplicate-agent warning never fired. Now scans past rejected matches.
  • Context.xml writes were non-atomic — both initial deploy and Ctrl+F10 redeploy used Files.writeString directly. New atomicWriteString helper (temp + atomic move) at both sites.
  • Bundled-app mirror produced malformed context.xml for directories containing -- — XML 1.0 forbids -- inside comments. Dir name is now sanitised before interpolation.
  • Liquibase cleanup missed under Turkish locale, multi-module artifact-to-module matching broken under tr_TR, and remote-deploy progress used JVM-default decimal separator — all pinned to Locale.ROOT.
  • Run-config editor leaked its message-bus listener — subscribeToRenameEvents now passes the editor as parent disposable so it auto-disconnects on disposeEditor.
  • ProcessCanceledException swallowed in five broad catches (credentials, notifications, run-config getState, Before-Launch sync) — PCE now rethrows; other exceptions still log and fall through.

Refactoring & tests

  • Extracted PortResolver from TomcatJavaParametersBuilder for independent testability.
  • 1546 tests, ~330 new this release. New test groups for PortResolver, BCEL/module-info compatibility, ECJ version compatibility, peer-aware port resolution, same-path conf/ refusal, manual-JDWP near-miss, manager-URL trailing slash, and the smart-error message-field regression.

Version 1.0.8

Resilience release — no new features; every change either reduces the surface area of future bugs or locks in a past fix with an end-to-end test.

  • Minimum IntelliJ version raised to 2025.1 — pluginSinceBuild 241 → 251, compile against 2025.1.7. Halves the verifier matrix without losing any capability (the 2026.1 dashboard builder API is not reachable from 2024.1/2025.1 anyway).
  • Services-panel state machine tightened — server state is now derived from a single authoritative function instead of scattered ad-hoc writes. Eliminates a class of regressions where fixing one handler broke another. The old over-aggressive "summary failure promotes every in-flight artifact to FAILED" behaviour is gone: real Tomcat emits that summary while later-successful contexts are still starting, and those contexts now show their true DEPLOYED state.
  • Self-healing for persisted-but-unregistered Tomcat references — when a run config references a Tomcat install that exists on disk but isn't in Application Servers (fresh IDE, VCS-imported project, wiped sandbox), the plugin now auto-registers it on first access instead of blocking Run. Broken references (missing directory, non-Tomcat path) still block with a clear error.
  • Integration test harness — canned Tomcat output fixtures now drive the full pipeline → lifecycle → status-service chain end-to-end, so cross-layer regressions can't hide behind analyzer-level unit tests.
  • Dashboard compat boundary simplified — dead speculative-reflection fallbacks removed; kept as a one-file boundary with a concrete migration checklist for the next floor bump.

Version 1.0.7

  • Debug mode breakpoints — JDWP agent is injected directly onto the JVM's VM parameters; the old path via GenericDebuggerRunner's patcher was silently bypassed.
  • Services panel mixed-success-as-success — a new summary-failure analyzer catches Tomcat's "One or more Contexts did not start successfully" messages and keeps the server state FAILED even when the per-artifact pattern can't name which artifact broke. Signaling is gated on this authoritative signal, not the generic error counter, so non-fatal SEVERE noise on healthy startups no longer causes false positives.
  • Cancellation vs. failure — user-cancelled remote deployments reset to PENDING instead of sticky-FAILED; manager-connection failures now mark every configured artifact as FAILED instead of leaving them stuck in DEPLOYING.
  • 2026.1 deprecation cleanup — 14 ReadAction.compute call sites migrated to a centralised helper; eliminates the scheduled-for-removal warnings against IU-261 while staying source-compatible with 2024.1+.

Version 1.0.6

  • Server tab overhaul — Configure… button preserves selection; canonical tab order (Code Coverage before Startup/Connection); single Show dialog checkbox replaces the duplicate pair; JavaScript debugger checkbox hidden on Community rather than shown disabled; layout migrated to VerticalLayout so form rows reflow correctly under font/theme changes; shared Configure… button helper removes copy-paste
  • "Deploy applications configured in Tomcat instance" now actually deploys them — new CatalinaHomeMirror hardlinks bundled WAR files and synthesizes per-app context descriptors for exploded web apps (zero file duplication, instant reflection of install-side changes). IDE artifacts always win context-path collisions; a manifest tracks placements so disabling the checkbox cleans up
  • "Allow parallel run" now isolates per launch — each parallel instance gets its own CATALINA_BASE under .runs/{runId}/ with auto-bumped ports; the rerun intercept correctly gates on isParallelRunEffective() (checkbox on and no pinned base) so pinned-base configs fall back to single-instance semantics instead of corrupting shared directories; base is cleaned up on process exit; refuses to delete pinned directories
  • Remote mode hardening — IPv6 manager URLs now supported end-to-end (basic [::1], IPv4-mapped, zone-qualified); URL validation delegates to java.net.URI as authoritative. Test Connection: generation-counter race protection drops stale results; status clears on any Host/Port/HTTPS/credential edit
  • Deployment tab — editing context path via the edit dialog now updates the browser URL (previously went stale). DeploymentArtifact.Source enum splits provenance (INTELLIJ_ARTIFACT/AUTO_DETECTED/EXTERNAL) from packaging (WAR/EXPLODED) — external sources are no longer falsely flagged as orphaned by the validator. External-source duplicate-path guard; packaging selector in edit dialog for EXTERNAL entries. Legacy type="external" configs migrate transparently
  • Logs tab persistence — deleting every log entry now survives reload (new logsSeeded marker distinguishes "fresh config" from "user emptied"); custom log paths pointed at different directories or renamed files are preserved on daily path-refresh instead of silently overwritten
  • Services panel hardening — scoped Run History and Startup Trends actions, human-readable startup times, error counts on failed nodes, navigation gated on DEPLOYED state
  • Data isolation — startup time tracker moved to project-level service; rename tracking migrates all stored data; deleted configs clear trend history
  • Shutdown noise fix — error/warning counters freeze during shutdown so Tomcat cleanup warnings don't inflate the Services badge
  • Thread safety — error/warning counters use AtomicInteger; state snapshots use defensive copies
  • Run history accuracy — artifact failures recorded even on exit code 0; non-zero shutdown preserves FAILED artifact states for post-mortem
  • Safety & refactoring — editor disposal guard, shared artifact matching utility, VM options configurator extraction, purpose-based producer naming, legacy LogFileConfig/LogsConfigurationTab retired in favour of IntelliJ's LogConfigurationPanel
  • Test coverage — 1218+ tests; covers parallel-run base isolation, CatalinaHomeMirror strategies, IPv6 URL forms (incl. IPv4-mapped + zone-qualified; IPvFuture documented unsupported), source/type split, log delete-all round-trip, deployment edit-dialog browser-URL propagation

Version 1.0.5

  • Configurable Build Artifacts task — "Build DevTomcat Artifacts" in Before Launch now shows a checkbox dialog listing all deployed artifacts for selection
  • ReadAction safety — all ArtifactManager/ModuleManager model access now wrapped in ReadAction.compute() across 5 files; prevents read-access violations on background threads
  • Config import fix — importing a configuration no longer silently wipes startup/shutdown scripts, passParentEnvs, or debug host/port; server mode changes now reconcile tab structure
  • EnvVarPanel fixes — passParentEnvs preserved on load; deleted computed keys can be re-added; Populate Defaults no longer resets the checkbox
  • ProcessStopSupport guard — descriptor cleanup failure no longer blocks relaunch; debug restart now shows balloon notification on failure
  • Atomic move fallback — TomcatConfigPreparer.atomicWriteString() now falls back to non-atomic replace when filesystem doesn't support ATOMIC_MOVE
  • Duplicate code elimination — extracted 7 reusable utilities replacing ~20 duplicated code blocks; replaced 28 inline FQN references with proper imports across 18 files
  • Test coverage — added EnvVarPanelStateTest (11 tests), TomcatDebuggerTest, TomcatApplicationUpdaterTest

Version 1.0.4

  • JRE Configuration dialog refactored — split into focused sub-dialogs for add/edit (JdkEditorDialog) and auto-detection (AutoDetectJdkDialog)
  • Startup/Connection tab — env var table and all related logic extracted to a new EnvVarPanel class; tab reduced from 1003 to 542 lines
  • Port resolution — inline 44-line block in TomcatJavaParametersBuilder.build() extracted to resolvePortsIfNeeded(); build sequence is now a clean 10-step method
  • VM Options field — replaced with IntelliJ's ExpandableTextField for proper handling of long option strings
  • Services panel — fixed issue where scrolling in the console could cause the Services panel to lose focus and auto-hide

Version 1.0.3

  • Multi-module Maven/Gradle deployment — Plugin now understands the IntelliJ module dependency graph. When a shared module is already packaged as a JAR in WEB-INF/lib, the plugin no longer adds a conflicting PreResources overlay. Eliminates Liquibase, CDI, and similar duplicate-classpath errors in multi-module projects. Detection uses three tiers: Maven artifactId name matching, file-content sampling, and Maven pom.properties metadata (works even for empty/uncompiled module outputs).
  • Duplicate deployment guard — Pre-launch validator warns when two artifacts share the same context path or the same physical deployment path, preventing silent 404s and double-startup overhead.
  • Restart failure notification — When a restart or mode-switch relaunch fails after the old process has already been stopped, a balloon notification is shown so the user knows Tomcat is no longer running and must be started manually.
  • Context path normalization fix — setContextPath("") now correctly stores "/" instead of an empty string, preventing incorrect duplicate-path detection and broken browser URLs.
  • Threading fixes — Fixed Read access is allowed from inside read-action only errors on multiple call sites: project load (ArtifactReferenceRefresher), post-build redeploy (LocalDeploymentStrategy — all model access now in a single ReadAction via ArtifactModelSnapshot), and configuration sync (syncBeforeLaunchWithDeployments).
  • API compatibility (IntelliJ 2025.x) — Replaced internal ExecutionManager.getRunningDescriptors(), deprecated UIUtil.getContextHelpForeground(), and ProgramRunnerUtil.executeConfiguration(). Added @Service level annotations to application and project services.
  • Stale artifact filtering — Artifacts left over from renamed or deleted modules are no longer shown in the artifact selector or auto-detected for deployment.

Version 1.0.2

  • Update Application on re-run — Run/Debug while Tomcat is running shows the Update dialog (Update Resources, Redeploy, Restart) instead of starting a duplicate process
  • Services toolbar actions — Update, Redeploy, and Restart are now one-click toolbar buttons in the Services panel
  • Redeploy preserves multi-module classpath — Redeploy now generates full context XML with PreResources/PostResources, matching initial deployment
  • Thread safety hardening — fixed race conditions in deployment notification, artifact count tracking, console debounce, and lifecycle history
  • Security improvements — URL scheme validation, path traversal protection on remote deploy, file size limit on config import
  • Resource leak fixes — listener cleanup on editor disposal, ProcessListener self-removal, port release on build failure

Version 1.0.0 — Initial Release

  • Full Tomcat lifecycle — run, debug, coverage, and redeploy from the IDE
  • Multi-artifact deployment with independent context paths
  • Smart Diagnostics — auto-detects 16+ Tomcat errors with actionable suggestions
  • Auto-port conflict resolution and CATALINA_BASE isolation
  • Live deployment status, history, and startup trends in Services panel
  • Update Running Application (Ctrl+F10) with frame deactivation support
  • Remote deployment via Tomcat Manager API
  • Configuration export/import for team sharing
